headline: Single-cell foundation models transfer ageing and regeneration signatures across species
label: Single Cell Foundation Model Embeddings
summary: Cross-species foundation model embeddings now map ageing and regenerative competence across mouse, human, fly, worm, and frog single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is transfer of learned cell representations across species and biological states. Two ageing studies test this directly: a cross-species adversarial domain adaptation workflow moves mouse ageing labels onto human haematopoietic stem cell and CD8+ T-cell scRNA and scATAC data, and fine-tuned scGPT and Geneformer models trained on roughly 1.3 million fly, worm, mouse and human cells recover a shared ribosomal-protein component alongside divergent age signatures. A third preprint uses species-native protein tokens in a frozen embedding that preserves homeolog features in allotetraploid Xenopus and links the representation to limb regenerative competence across frog and mouse. A published Unify study adds universal multimodal embeddings that combine RNA, protein, and language-model features into cross-species cell embeddings. What is new is the use of foundation-model embeddings as the common carrier for cross-species comparison of ageing and regeneration. The items differ in how far they report controlled generalization testing, so this thread should not be read as uniform.
